newsitem.title: CANADA: Home construction boosts 1996 building permits.
newsitem.headline: Home construction boosts 1996 building permits.

text.p: A rebound in residential construction intentions in 1996 helped push up the value of building permits issued during the year by 6.4 percent compared to 1995, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Municipalities issued C$26.2 billion in building permits for the year, the agency said.

The gain stemmed mainly from a sharp rise in building permits for the housing sector, which jumped 18.7 percent to C$15.6 billion. But the gain only partially offset the 24.7 percent slide in 1995, the agency said.
The strong performance in the housing sector was the result of historically low mortgage rates and stronger demand for new and existing homes, Statscan said.

"The upward trend displayed in the residential sector since August 1995 suggests further growth for the new home market, should mortgage rates and house prices remain relatively stable," the agency said.
But the non-residential sector fell 8.1 percent in 1996 to C$10.4 billion, after two straight years of increases, Statscan said.
The downturn came mainly from a sharp drop in the institutional component, which fell 27.9 percent to C$2.2 billion in 1996, the lowest in 12 years.
"This was consistent with spending cutbacks announced by all levels of government," Statistics Canada said.
